selection.rule: least recently reviewed with rotation-order tie break

pue.boundary: Google global large-scale data-center fleet after stable operation; not isolated to external Google Cloud AI workloads
pue.basis: Reported operational fleet PUE was 1.09 TTM and 1.10 for Q2. No matched architecture- and workload-weighted external GCP AI PUE was disclosed, so no PUE is selected for the economic model.
pue.aggregation_rule: Use IT-energy weighting only when cohort IT energy and matched PUE become available.

model.revenue_scope: Recognized external GCP AI compute-service revenue excluding Workspace, security and data services, non-AI GCP, TPU system sales, internal workloads and backlog
model.capacity_time_basis: 91-day quarter; additions enter only when active and are weighted by days active

formulas.revenue_per_it_mw_year: annualized recognized external GCP AI compute-service revenue / period-average active external GCP AI IT MW
formulas.revenue_per_effective_it_mw_year: annualized recognized external GCP AI compute-service revenue / (period-average active external GCP AI IT MW * physical utilization)
formulas.ironwood_list_revenue_per_chip_year: published dollars per chip-hour * 8760; this is not a MW metric without full-system allocated power

assumptions.basis: Simple annualization of one quarter; diagnostic only and not a forecast.
The reported 1.09 TTM fleet PUE has a broader perimeter than external GCP AI and is not substituted into the model.
TPU pricing accrues while resources are ready, but paid reservation occupancy and physical utilization are not disclosed.
Google discloses pod topology but not matched allocated server, interconnect, storage and networking power per chip.

rejected_shortcuts: Do not divide total Google Cloud revenue by a capacity figure; the segment includes Workspace, security, data services, non-AI GCP and TPU system sales.
Do not divide revenue or joint-venture equity by the Blackstone project's future 500 MW; it is not Q2 active capacity and its power boundary is not defined.
Do not apply global fleet PUE to external GCP AI without matched IT-energy weights.
Do not divide chip-hour price by chip TDP; IT MW requires allocated full-system power and cohort mix.
Do not treat RPO, contracted obligations or financing proceeds as recognized revenue.

token_economics.reason: The reviewed primary sources do not disclose matched realized token prices, saleable token volume, model mix or energy per token for Google Cloud.

structured_deals.name: SpaceX Google Compute Agreement
structured_deals.status: contracted; service ramp scheduled through September 2026
structured_deals.economic_effect: Creates an $11.04 billion annualized payment stream at full monthly run rate, but the payment covers a broader infrastructure bundle and may be terminated after 2026 with notice.
structured_deals.term: Monthly payments October 2026 through June 2029 after ramp through September 2026; either party may terminate after December 31, 2026 on 90 days' notice.
structured_deals.boundary: Payments cover approximately 110,000 NVIDIA GPUs plus CPUs, memory and other infrastructure and are not a pure GPU price or a MW-normalized result.

structured_deals.name: Blackstone-Google TPU cloud joint venture
structured_deals.economic_effect: Provides $5 billion of initial counterparty equity toward 500 MW of future capacity while leaving the power boundary and Google's recognized revenue undisclosed.
structured_deals.term: Initial capacity expected online in 2027; Google supplies TPU hardware, software and services.
structured_deals.boundary: The stated 500 MW is a future project boundary that is not defined as IT or facility load. Equity per stated MW is not total project capex or Google revenue.

structured_deals.name: Technical-infrastructure, energy and data-center commitments
structured_deals.economic_effect: Secures long-dated capacity and supply but creates large fixed-payment, termination, guarantee and VIE-backstop exposure whose Cloud/AI allocation is not disclosed.
structured_deals.term: Energy agreements extend as late as 2054 and can include take-or-pay provisions and termination fees.
structured_deals.boundary: Alphabet consolidated commitments; Cloud/AI attribution is not disclosed. RPO and obligations are not revenue.

structured_deals.name: H1 2026 debt and AI financing
structured_deals.economic_effect: Raises $49.5 billion of disclosed common and preferred equity proceeds plus $51.8 billion of senior debt issuance, increasing financing capacity while introducing dilution, coupons and a $1.1875 billion preferred annual dividend run rate.
structured_deals.term: Preferred dividend rate 6.25%; conversion and maturity terms are instrument-specific.
structured_deals.boundary: Corporate financing supports Alphabet's investment program but is not fully attributable to external GCP AI.

findings: Google Cloud generated $24.768 billion of Q2 2026 revenue and $8.814 billion of operating income, but the segment perimeter is too broad for an external AI-compute numerator.
TPU system sales entered recognized Cloud revenue in Q2 and mostly shift existing system agreements into 2027, yet management said Cloud growth accelerated meaningfully even excluding those sales.
Reported fleet PUE was 1.09 TTM and 1.10 in Q2; neither is a matched external GCP AI measurement.
Ironwood list prices imply $105,120 per chip-year on demand and $47,304 under a three-year commitment, but a defensible $/MW baseline remains impossible without allocated full-system power per chip.

Alphabet has assembled a capital stack spanning obligations, leases, guarantees, VIE backstops, debt, equity and partner financing; these lower near-term capacity constraints while increasing fixed-commitment and dilution exposure.
